mechanism_narrative: The collapse then sharp rebound in WORKPLACES from -53.3 to -18.9 over two weeks marks the end of the holiday-and-Omicron office shutdown; returning commuter volume restores weekday foot traffic in retail corridors, lifting mean RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks above the -23.6 mean of the last four.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose 29.7 points between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages at or below -23.6 over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to improve week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated GROCERY_PHARM (25.0 at t-3w decaying to 11.3) reflects substitution of discretionary spend toward essential provisioning under transmission risk. Once the weekly GROCERY_PHARM mean drops below 8.0, that substitution reverses and discretionary retail recaptures the wallet share within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean falls below 8.0 from 11.3 at t-0w
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 25.0 to 11.3 across the four-week window
regime_hint: steady state with declining transmission risk
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 8.0 yet RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-28-day mean within the following two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT is the fastest-confirming revealed-preference signal of out-of-home activity. Its first weekly improvement in the window (+7.2 points, from -46.1 to -38.9) precedes retail footfall recovery, so any further week-on-week TRANSIT gain should propagate into RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 5 points week-on-week above its t-0w level of -38.9
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 7.2 points in the final week
failure_condition: TRANSIT posts a further gain greater than 5 points week-on-week while RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the same two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Retail recovery requires both trip generation and destination demand: TRANSIT supply of trips and WORKPLACES supply of daytime population must rise together. Their joint improvement in the final week (-38.9 and -18.9) is multiplicative, so retail footfall accelerates over four weeks only while both series keep improving in the same week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve week-on-week in the same observation week
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improved in the final week after three weeks of decline
regime_hint: reopening with returning commuting and trip demand
failure_condition: Weeks where TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve jointly are followed by four-week RETAIL_REC means no higher than weeks where either series alone improves.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL above baseline is the direct measure of time reallocated away from commercial venues. Its decline from 15.9 to 10.0 signals that home-confinement behavior is unwinding, which mechanically releases consumption hours back to retail venues within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 12.0 from 10.0 at t-0w
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL dropped 5.9 points from t-1w to t-0w
regime_hint: behavioral normalization after a stay-at-home surge
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL stays below 12.0 for a full week while RETAIL_REC fails to rise relative to the prior week.

mechanism_narrative: The last-28-day RETAIL_REC mean of -23.6 is depressed by the Boxing Day and New Year trough of -31.1 at t-2w. Southern-hemisphere summer holidays end in late January, so the next 28-day window is seasonally cleaner and should exceed the holiday-contaminated baseline even without any epidemiological change.
evidence_refs: fact:t-2w RETAIL_REC of -31.1 is the window minimum and falls inside the last-28-day comparison window
regime_hint: post-holiday seasonal normalization in the southern-hemisphere summer
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days averages below -23.6, the holiday-contaminated last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Victoria's Omicron-era density and capacity caps bind hardest on seated hospitality and indoor recreation, which are counted inside RETAIL_REC. Easing or expiry of those caps while case growth turns negative releases suppressed demand, so retail should climb over two weeks in that policy regime.
candidate_trigger: Victorian density limits are lifted or statewide case growth turns negative while TRANSIT holds above -45
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC floor of -31.1 coincides with the deepest TRANSIT trough of -46.9
regime_hint: policy easing under falling case counts
failure_condition: Density limits are lifted and case growth is negative, yet the two-week RETAIL_REC mean does not exceed -23.6.

mechanism_narrative: If the Omicron transmission peak holds households at home, the co-movement of RESIDENTIAL above 12 with TRANSIT below -35 sustains voluntary avoidance that outlasts mandates. In that regime retail trips are deferred rather than pent up, and the next four weeks print below the last four.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays at or above 12.0 while TRANSIT stays at or below -35.0 for a full week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL peaked at 15.9 while TRANSIT was -46.1 at t-1w
regime_hint: active Omicron transmission peak with voluntary self-restriction
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL remains at or above 12.0 with TRANSIT at or below -35.0, yet RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its last-28-day mean of -23.6.
